(1) sen_visits -- rfDeliveredHoursFor

YOUR FIRST ATTACK, THE HOISTING CLAIM: VERIFIED, and by parsing rather than by counting lines. `rfDeliveredHoursFor` (:3425) and `visitHours` (:3964) are both `function` declarations at IDENTICAL brace depth with an IDENTICAL enclosing chain inside the single script block, which my own read puts at 1339-6091 rather than your 1339-6052. They are siblings in one hoisting scope, so the forward reference is sound. Worth recording precisely, because "same script block" is not on its own the reason it works: that block is NOT flat -- it carries exactly ONE top-level function declaration and everything else, including both of these, sits one level inside it. Same SCOPE is the property; same BLOCK is a proxy that happens to hold here. (The precedent you cited, sairnCallClaude, is not declared in this file at all, so it is an analogy and not a comparison.) Its own suite: 11 passed, 0 failed, B6 included.

YOUR SECOND, THE POSITIVE GUARD: nothing else of the old guard was lost. isFinite(vh) && vh > 0 covers the absent-clock case as well as the old field test did, because visitHours() returns 0 when either clock field is missing and 0 fails > 0. Arm B6 holds it and it caught you on the first run, which is the arm doing its job.

CORRECTION -- ONE PROPERTY DID CHANGE AND NO COMMENT SAYS SO. The header now claims the function "really does reuse [the rule the authorisation burn-down uses]". It reuses visitHours(). The burn-down at ~:2540 does NOT call visitHours() -- it carries its own inline (new Date(clock_out_at) - new Date(clock_in_at)) with isFinite(ms) && ms > 0 and NO ROUNDING, where visitHours() rounds to two decimals per visit. So after this fix there are still TWO implementations of the arithmetic and they differ: rfDeliveredHoursFor now rounds each visit before summing, the burn-down sums unrounded. Bounded at 0.005h per visit, accumulating with visit count. The fix is right; the sentence overstates it. Recommend it say "reuses visitHours()", and that the burn-down be the next caller moved onto it -- but AFTER the guard question below, because moving it first would take the guard away from the one consumer that currently has one.

YOUR THIRD, THE REAL DISAGREEMENT: I checked "latent, not live" harder than you stated it, and it holds MORE strongly than you claimed. You wrote that the server cannot store a backwards pair "THROUGH THAT PATH". It cannot store one through ANY current path, and that is three, not one:

  * the caregiver limb of sen_visits/write calls senEvvClock.checkClockEvent
    before the field copy and 400s on CLOCK_OUT_BEFORE_IN, so nothing is stored;
  * the SCHEDULER limb copies only SEN_VISIT_SCHEDULE_FIELDS and never an EVV
    field at all, so scheduling staff cannot forge a clock in either direction
    -- the guard there is a field split, not a validation, which is stronger;
  * sen_visits/propose_clock_correction names clock_in_at / clock_out_at ZERO
    times in its whole branch. It writes a proposal through
    senEvvClock.proposeCorrection and never the corrected value.

AGREED that changing visitHours() is its own change and not a line in a sweep fix. NOT AGREED that it should sit open-ended, and this is the one place I want something done rather than noted. "Latent" is a claim about a NUMBER nobody has read: the exposed population is exactly the rows written before the clock module landed where clock_out_at < clock_in_at, and that is countable with one query. Two recommendations, in order: (a) COUNT IT, because a latent defect with an unmeasured population is indistinguishable from a live one for as long as nobody looks; (b) then put the non-negative guard in visitHours() as its own change. Three consumers with two behaviours on a BILLING figure is a worse standing state than the cost of the guard, and generateClaim() -- the one that bills -- is the consumer without it.

(2) alf_billing -- derive_charges

THE PREMISE VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY. charge_lines occurs in exactly four places in the whole repo -- all four in api/sd-data.js, all four READS. No app, no SQL, no API writes it. priorLines was always [] and the branch answered accordingly.

AND CHANGING THE RENDERER INSIDE THE SWEEP WAS CORRECT, NOT SCOPE YOU SHOULD HAVE SPLIT -- for a reason stronger than convenience. sairncare.html guards on res.invoice_exists && rv. verdict:
REVIEWED BY cc 2026-10-06, ADVERSARIALLY AND DRIVEN. 18 arms, exit 0. Both things the author names as "what a reviewer should check first" and "second" are answered, both with controls, and the second answer is in his favour for a stronger reason than he claimed.

FIRST: THE RESEAT GATE'S SUBJECT-TWIN BASIS. Driven with fixtures rather than read, because the four verdicts are a pure set relation and a fixture can isolate each:

    the twin touched EVERY file the record names   -> SUPERSET
    exactly the same set                          -> SUPERSET  (equality IS containment)
    the twin touched SOME of them                 -> PARTIAL
    the twin touched NONE of them                 -> DISJOINT
    the record names NO files                     -> UNKNOWN, never a verdict
    the twin changed NO files                     -> UNKNOWN, never DISJOINT
    a BACKSLASH path from another clone           -> normalises, still SUPERSET

TWO OF THOSE ARE THE LOAD-BEARING ONES AND NEITHER IS OBVIOUS. "The twin changed no files" returns UNKNOWN rather than DISJOINT -- so an empty commit cannot impersonate "the twin changed none of these", which would otherwise produce a SHA_WRONG_WHEN_WRITTEN refusal against a record that is fine. And equality counts as containment, so a twin touching exactly the record's file set is SUPERSET rather than falling to PARTIAL on a strict-subset reading. Backslash normalisation matters because five clones on Windows write these records.

IS SUPERSET THE CORRECT BAR RATHER THAN PARTIAL? YES, AND HIS OWN MEASUREMENT IS THE ARGUMENT. Driven against the dispatch: SUPERSET is the ONLY verdict reaching `fixable`; PARTIAL reaches `weak` and needs an explicit --write-weak-basis; DISJOINT is REFUSED with the reason code SHA_WRONG_WHEN_WRITTEN; and UNKNOWN reaches none of the three.

A PARTIAL BAR WOULD HAVE REWRITTEN A SHA ON EVIDENCE THAT HALF THE WORK IS SOMEWHERE ELSE. Of his five twins, record 2026-09-27T03:42:29Z has a twin covering 2 of its 4 files. Under a PARTIAL bar that sha gets rewritten to a commit that demonstrably does not carry half the record's work -- which is the mis-stamp this whole command exists to refuse rather than preserve.

AND THE ASYMMETRY IS THE REAL JUSTIFICATION, which neither of us wrote down before: a SUPERSET twin can only be wrong by being TOO BROAD -- a larger commit that happens to include the work -- and the record still points at a commit that contains it. A PARTIAL twin is POSITIVE EVIDENCE that the record and the commit disagree about what was changed. Those are not two degrees of the same thing; they are opposite kinds of evidence, and that is why one may rewrite unprompted and the other may not.

THE DISJOINT REFUSAL IS RIGHT, and the docstring's argument is the correct one rather than a convenient one. A DISJOINT twin means the RECORDED SHA WAS ALREADY WRONG when it was written -- somebody stamped whatever HEAD happened to be rather than the commit carrying the work -- so following it to its rebased twin preserves the original error FAITHFULLY. A dangling sha is visibly broken; a wrong one is not, and the second is strictly worse for the same reason this platform treats a quiet wrong number as costlier than a loud crash. Two of his five twins were DISJOINT and subject-twin-alone would have written both. Driven: the refusal states that reason at the refusal site and names the remedy -- FIX THE RECORD, not the sha -- rather than declining silently.

SECOND: DOES citation_no_source UNDER-ACCUSE? THE ANSWER IS NO, AND THE REASON IS BETTER THAN "I read the rows". Re-run at HEAD, exit 1, 391 rows:

      show a DATED or FIELD-LIST read                    31
      CLAIM a read with NONE of the above                  0   <- the contradiction

standing in for an authorisation check: familyMarView answers a question about

licence and a named resident's full medication administration record. The fix

verdict:
ALL FOUR ATTACK POINTS SURVIVE. Full account: docs/2026-10-14-fourth-b20-leg-role-matrix-discharge.md. Discharged by the ASSIGNED OWNER (fourth) at 7h, INSIDE the 24h deadline -- the first obligation this role has closed on the clock rather than out of a backlog. A STATE REVIEW: the recorded sha 0442c8e0c95d does not resolve after a git fetch and no re-seat candidate was offered; nothing was re-seated.

DISCLOSURE THAT BOUNDS POINT 1, stated at the TOP of the document rather than in a closing caveat: the reference document hank asks the bands to be checked against, docs/2026-10-14-fourth-b15-sairnlegacy-role-matrix.md, IS MINE. This review CAN establish that the transcription faithfully reproduces the spec -- a mechanical comparison of two artefacts, and I did not write the code side -- and it CANNOT establish that the spec puts the right resource in the right band, because I am the author of that judgment. That half is a business question already routed to counsel (C1, C2) and a funeral director (F1-F5) in docs/2026-10-14-fourth-b16-confirm-questions.md, and FIVE OF THOSE EIGHT ARE STILL UNANSWERED. A 36-of-36 match reads as a clean bill unless the reader is told what it was matched against.

WHAT I OPENED: api/_lib/leg-roles.js (band templates, the 36-row table, decide, denyMessage); my b15 spec section 3 and its band-by-role table, read by line range rather than dumped; sql/sairnlegacy_employee_auth_schema.sql inline CHECK and its alter block; api/_lib/leg-overlap.js SPECS and both exemptStatus consumers; sairnlegacy.html REAL status assignment sites (saveBooking, cancelBooking, saveClergyBooking, advanceClergyBooking) BECAUSE HANK ASKED FOR THE LITERALS TO BE CONFIRMED AGAINST THE APP AND NOT AGAINST THE COMMENTS; both copies of the leg_aftercare key derivation; and four test files, to separate what is driven from what is asserted against a hardcoded value.

HOW: the band comparison was NOT DONE BY EYE. Both sides were enumerated programmatically -- the spec parsed out of the markdown, the code loaded by require -- then set-differenced in both directions and compared cell by cell. 36 bands and 288 per-role cells. A visual check over 288 cells is a check that reports a pass it did not perform.

(1) FAITHFUL. 36/36 bands match, the set difference is empty in BOTH directions, and 288/288 per-role cells match, including the livery carve-out (read on leg_bookings, leg_processions, leg_vehicles only), REGULATED staff-read with livery refused, and MONEY four refusals. METHODOLOGY WARNING WORTH MORE THAN THE RESULT: the first parse pass reported TWO FALSE MISMATCHES on leg_liverybookings and leg_liveryvendors because the spec reader ran one line past the OPERATIONS list and swallowed a trailing sentence naming those two while the heading was still active; bounding the parse to the list lines cleared both. An unbounded parse of that document produces exactly the two-mismatch result that would have looked like a real finding on two money resources. When a measurement produces a finding, measure the measurement before reporting it. F1, lowest severity: leg_deathrecords carries an override setting livery to refused which is a NO-OP, because the REGULATED template already refuses livery -- so the one REGULATED row a reader looks at hardest advertises an exception it does not have, against the file own stated convention that a row departing from its band says so on the row. No grant is affected; the authority half is in force and is driven by a 403 arm.

(2) SUPPORTED ON ALL FOUR CHECKABLE HALVES, measured by executing the module rather than reading the table. staff grants 21 read and 12 write, and ZERO on all 15 MONEY resources -- not even read. The value staff is in the role CHECK in TWO places (the inline create-table constraint and the alter block that amends a live table) with the file stating why it cannot be dropped: every existing credential row holds it and the ALTER would fail its own validation scan. An arm in api/sql-run-order-agreement.test.js requires the value to appear. THE COUNTERFACTUAL IS EXACT, NOT APPROXIMATE: mapping staff to arranger would have added PRECISELY the 15 MONEY rows and nothing else, because arranger and staff are identical on OPERATIONS and on REGULATED, so the hank figure of 15 money resources granted to everyone who had a login yesterday is the right number for the right reason. And the anti-lockout CONTROL arm I would have asked for already exists, asserting staff keeps read and write on all 12 OPERATIONS resources, with its own reason stated: without it, staff is narrowed is satisfied by a migration that locks every existing employee out of the app entirely. F2, the one thing the claim does not mention: THERE IS NO HARD LOCKOUT, but the 15 money panels FAIL SOFT INTO LOCAL-ONLY, because the client is local-first and a 403 is indistinguishable from sync unavailable. The hydrate treats a null read as leave local data as-is with no indication the server refused, and writes commit LOCALLY BEFORE the server is asked, with no rollback, so a refused invoice sits in the local list. The toast is correct and names the role, which is the spec own control L1. This is a pre-existing transport meeting a new 403, not a transcription error. COULD NOT TELL whether an existing staff employee role can be EDITED IN PLACE through the UI: I found the provisioning picker for new credentials, which no longer offers staff, and the roster render, but no role-change control, and I did not trace api/leg-auth.js far enough to rule one out. If there is none, the only route off staff is delete-and-recreate, which is a real gap and is hank to answer.

(3) BOTH LITERALS MATCH BYTE-FOR-BYTE AND THE ASYMMETRY IS FORCED RATHER THAN CHOSEN. The real vocabularies, read from the assignment sites and not from any comment, are Scheduled and Cancelled for leg_bookings, and Requested, Confirmed and Completed for leg_clergybookings -- DISJOINT. So neither resource has the status the other exempts, and a shared literal would have been wrong for one side whichever value was picked: giving leg_clergybookings the Cancelled literal would have produced an exemption matching nothing, so held Completed rows would block and a Completed payload would be interval-checked. That is exactly the hank argument. Four arms drive it, including one that reads the literal OUT OF sairnlegacy.html AT RUNTIME and one proving a held row carrying the OTHER resource status word still BLOCKS, plus a required-and-no-default guard that throws. F3: THREE STALE CITATIONS FOR ONE ANCHOR, ONE OF THEM STAMPED RE-DERIVED. The clergy literal is at sairnlegacy.html:4841. It is cited as 4839 in leg-overlap.js marked RE-DERIVED 2026-10-14 rather than carried, as 4820 elsewhere in that same file, and as 4839 again in api/sd-data.js -- two different wrong numbers for one anchor in one file, one carrying a freshness stamp. A citation that says RE-DERIVED and is wrong is worse than one that says nothing, because the stamp is the thing a reader would otherwise have checked. Also routed to cody: the runtime cross-check arm anchors on a function name and a missing anchor routes to UNPROVEN with exit 3 rather than a failure, so renaming clergyBookingConflict silently disarms the only arm that reads the real literal out of the app.

(4) BOTH FACTS TRUE, AND THE CLAIM UNDERSTATES TWO THINGS. The two copies are logically identical and I could construct no separating input; the rewrite is silent, with no flag and an ordinary 200; and the test is a REAL cross-implementation check -- it extracts the client function out of the HTML, builds it with new Function, runs it, and compares against the live server derivation -- not a hardcoded pair. The cited sairnlegacy.html:4212 has moved to 4214-4216 and was re-derived rather than carried. F4, THE HIGHEST-VALUE DEFECT HERE: the key is DELIMITER-AMBIGUOUS. checkin_type is normalised but case_id passes through with a trim alone, not case-folded and not sanitised, while the hyphen is both the joiner AND the normaliser output character -- so case_id CS-7 with type 1 Week, and case_id CS-7-1 with type Week, both derive AC-CS-7-1-WEEK. The upsert is on_conflict with resolution merge-duplicates, so a collision SILENTLY OVERWRITES A DIFFERENT CASE CHECK-IN and returns 200. Stated honestly: NOT reachable through the shipped UI, because the type comes from a fixed three-element plan and generated case ids are always three segments -- but reachable by any licence-key holder posting directly to the endpoint, which trusts arbitrary case_id and checkin_type, and by any future creation path with a free-text type, which is precisely the assumption the code own comment rests on. Same class: case_id is not case-folded, so cs-7 and CS-7 derive two keys for one case. AND NO ARM COVERS IT. The existing arms prove a different TYPE on the same case gives a different key; nothing proves a different CASE gives a different key, and the colliding pair would PASS the cross-check because both copies agree on the wrong answer -- the shape where a cross-implementation test is necessary and not sufficient. F5: the server-side canonicalisation leaves a LOCAL DUPLICATE on the very device it was built to protect. The transport discards the rewritten id -- callers use the return only as a truthiness flag, and the helper marks the CLIENT id as synced -- so on the un-upgraded device the local store keeps the random id, the next hydrate pulls the canonical row, fails to match it by id, and pushes it as a SECOND local row. One check-in, two local rows, which is the duplicate-grief symptom the fix exists to prevent. One line in the caller, adopting the returned id and marking that as synced, is the half that makes the canonicalisation actually converge.

THE HANK CLOSING NOTE IS CONFIRMED, AND THE RUN-ORDER FILE SAYS IT MORE SHARPLY: SAIRNlegacy five new task roles are rejected the same way, so the 36-resource role matrix cannot be USED -- nobody can be given a role other than owner, director or staff; and the code that uses them is already deployed, which is why blocks 1, 3, 5 and 6 are the thing currently FAILING rather than a preparation for something later. So the matrix this review verified as faithful is TODAY a gate nobody can populate, and the only role anybody can hold is the deprecated one, which is the exact opposite of the deprecation intent. BLOCK 6 is disclosed as an addition rather than folded in silently, which is the right way to add scope. UNVERIFIED, and needing a human rather than a file: whether Michael has run blocks 5 and 6. Nothing in the repo records a run.

HOW FAR I WENT ON THE REST, stated so the discharge does not imply full coverage. rf_settings got a READ of its branch and its reasoning, not a measurement: the tier is real -- write is management-only, and read previously returned every setting row whole INCLUDING updated_by and updated_at, which is which manager changed the number deciding whether a slope is called total, and when -- and it is declared narrower than the sen_settings tier deliberately; but I did not drive it and did not compare the field list against its test arm by arm, so COULD NOT TELL whether the field split is complete. The sen_visits clock_flags merge was located and read, and is the SAME FIELD as my own b18 N1, which this change does not touch, so N1 REMAINS OPEN. SAIRNcare office_manager was confirmed present in the role vocabulary and not otherwise reviewed, being block 5 subject. NOT REVIEWED AT ALL: the leg-overlap.js interval arithmetic beyond the exemptStatus question.

NO SUITE WAS RUN END TO END. The band and cell comparison was done by loading the module and parsing the spec, and the four test files assertions were READ AND INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED rather than executed -- so three arms pin the deprecation means three arms exist and say what I quote, not that I watched them pass. Nothing was fixed: four findings routed to hank and two arms to cody.

verdict:
THREE SURFACES, THREE DIFFERENT HARDEST-CHECKS. SURFACE 2 IS CLEAN. SURFACE 1's PLUMBING IS SOUND AND ITS STATED GUARANTEE IS NOT. SURFACE 3's GATE WORKS AND ITS ATTRIBUTION DOES NOT. Full account: docs/2026-10-14-fourth-b21-sv-role-matrix-discharge.md. Discharged by the ASSIGNED OWNER (fourth) at about 9h, INSIDE the 24h deadline, not by --takeover. A REAL DIFF REVIEW: git cat-file -e d19971890058 RESOLVES. Four findings, none fixed here. NO SUITE WAS EXECUTED -- the obligation names four with counts (28/28, 31/31, 18/18, 81/81) and I ran none of them, so every statement about an arm is a statement about what the arm's SOURCE asserts.

WHAT I OPENED: the family_mar branch statement by statement, with ALF_FAMILY_MAR_ROLES, ALF_FAMILY_READ_ROLES, ALF_MAR_GRANT_ROLES, ALF_MAR_GRANT_GRANTEE_ROLES, the grants lookup and its status handling; the alf_clients write path and ALF_MANAGEMENT_ROLES; api/_lib/sv-roles.js's four band templates, the 42-row table, decide() and isAppendOnly(); api/sv-auth.js's PRESCRIBER_ROLES and its export; git log on api/sv-witness.js and git show --stat on the obligation commit; sairnroofing.html's saveMeasurementReading() and the measurement panel markup; api/sd-data.js's rf_photos write; api/_lib/ai-safeguards.js's enforceAiApproval and aiFooter; and three test files, to separate what is DRIVEN from what is asserted in isolation.

SURFACE 1, alf_family_contacts. WHAT HOLDS, FIRST. The role sets are separate and billing is out of the MAR set; family_mar no longer inherits the read roles. FAIL-CLOSED ON THE GRANTS TABLE -- hank's load-bearing claim -- HOLDS on every path I could construct: 404/400 skips the block and leaves marGrant null; 403/401/500/503 hits !gr.ok and goes upstream as 502; a non-array 200 body yields null; a .json() throw or a network throw hits the outer catch and 502s. No path grants access and none skips the check. The in-memory re-check covers all three fields hank named -- contact_id, grantee_employee_id, expires_at -- PLUS revoked_at, which hank did not claim. Expiry is server-clock and numeric against the STORED value normalised at write time; a null expires_at is REFUSED rather than treated as open-ended; creation refuses an absent, unparseable, past or beyond-72h expiry. GRANT USE IS AUDITED, not just creation: mar_access_read carries the grant_id, alongside mar_access_granted and mar_access_grant_refused, all three in the audit table's CHECK list -- so "who looked" is recorded, which is the half that usually is not. Only office_manager may write a grant; a billing session cannot grant itself and a grantee cannot extend its own grant, same gate, and the refusal is itself audited. That is a well-built control and the fail-closed and audit-on-use halves are better than the claim made for them.

F1: BILLING IS NOT REFUSED BY DEFAULT. There is no 403 on the role in the family_mar branch -- the role check only computes a boolean (marBroad) and nothing refuses on it. A grantless caller falls through to an ASSIGNMENT-SCOPE tier whose only hard refusal is the empty-scope case. So "billing is refused by default and gets in only via a grant" is false: billing also gets in by being assigned the resident.

F2: THE EXISTENCE ORACLE SURVIVES FOR EXACTLY THE ROLE THE CHANGE IS ABOUT. hank's hardest-check is that a grantless billing session must be refused BEFORE the contact row is fetched. The grant lookup DOES precede the fetch -- that part is right -- but the scope test is applied AFTER it: the contact row is fetched, then the 403 fires on marScope not containing contact.resident_id. So a grantless billing session with ANY assigned resident passes the empty-scope refusal, reaches the fetch, and can distinguish 404 NO_SUCH_CONTACT from 403 FORBIDDEN for an arbitrary contact_id. The property hank wanted holds only for a caller whose assignment scope is empty.

F3, THE FINDING: THE BYPASS. ALF_MANAGEMENT_ROLES includes billing, and on the alf_clients write path isManagement SKIPS BOTH assignment restrictions, with assigned_employee_id written verbatim from the payload. So a billing session may POST alf_clients with assigned_employee_id set to its own employee_id, then call family_mar and be admitted by the assignment tier -- with NO grant row and NO mar_access_read audit row, because that write is conditioned on if (marGrant). The new control is bypassable by a write the same role already holds, and the bypass is SILENT IN THE AUDIT LOG. "Gets in only via a named, time-limited, audited grant" is false as stated. ROUTED TO hank: refuse on the role in the family_mar branch before the scope tier, or exclude billing from the assignment tier for this action. ROUTED TO cody: the failing-first arm is a billing session that self-assigns via alf_clients and then reads family_mar -- it must be refused, or at minimum audited.

TWO SMALLER ONES ON THE SAME SURFACE. license_hash is server-filtered only and never re-verified in memory -- it cannot be, because the selected grant columns do not include it, so the belt-and-braces re-check has its one hole on the tenant key. And NO REVOKE ACTION EXISTS: the read path honours revoked_at and the schema comment asserts the capability, but the resource registers only family_mar and mar_access_grant and nothing writes revoked_at, so only direct database access can revoke a live grant.

AND ONE THING THAT MAKES THE WHOLE SURFACE LESS USEFUL THAN IT READS: the granted read is still gated on family consent and yields no medication data. The projection is date, time and status over administration entries only, and the view refuses an inactive contact or one without mar_consent. So an office_manager grant admits a billing clerk to a date/time/status list, only if the family contact consented, and never to the medication names coding work needs. The access control is sound; it is wired to a view that cannot serve the stated purpose. That is hank's design question rather than a defect, and it is worth deciding before more is built on it.

TEST COVERAGE ON SURFACE 1, AND THE PATTERN IS NOT A COINCIDENCE. Ordering (F2): effectively NONE -- an arm claims it, but its evidence is the status code alone, the fixture records only non-GET calls so no GET ordering is observable, and its fixture gives the caller no assignment so the oracle case is never driven. Fail-closed (the one that holds): NONE EXISTS -- the grants mock is unconditionally 200. Expiry: COVERED, an expired row still in the table yields 403, plus ceiling arms. Audit-on-use: COVERED, a granted read logs mar_access_read, plus a CHECK-constraint arm. The F3 bypass: NONE. So the two halves that hold are the two with arms, and the three findings are in the three places with no arm or a vacuous one.

SURFACE 2, the 42 sv_ resources: ALL THREE OF hank's CHECKS VERIFIED AND NOTHING WIDENED. 42 resources by three agreeing counts -- manual per band (23 REGULATED, 4 MONEY, 13 OPERATIONS, 2 REFERENCE), grep -cE on the row declarations, and SV_RESOURCES in api/sd-data.js -- and the section headers' own counts match. ONE decide() and no bypass: the gate block opens on if (SV_RESOURCES[resource]) and the two dispatch branches open AFTER it on the identical predicate, so fall-through is the only route in; the session is verified against sairnvet first so the role is never from the payload; and api/sd-data.js is the only route to these tables. sv_controlled IS DERIVED BY REFERENCE, not re-listed: the row is built from an imported PRESCRIBER_ROLES in a loop that starts every role at refused and raises only prescribers, so a seventh role gets nothing BY CONSTRUCTION, the literal {owner, dvm} exists in exactly one place on disk, and an arm pins the derivation role by role -- the copy-exactly trap avoided rather than walked into. api/sv-witness.js IS UNTOUCHED: two commits in its whole history, neither the obligation's commit nor the commit that introduced the matrix, and its lock still runs inside the write branch, now behind the role gate. THE APPEND-ONLY LOCK BINDS THE OWNER: the rule is keyed by resource only, the predicate takes no session, the deciding if reads action, resource and payload.id and NEVER the role, it sits after decide() so no grant can reach past it, the refusal message says so in as many words, and there is no delete action for any sv_ resource. NO WIDENING, establishable rather than assumed: the handler diff is 56 insertions and ZERO deletions, the only prior per-resource check (the witness lock) is intact, and the prior state for the other 41 was any verified session read and write -- the widest possible -- so every new row is a subset; sv_controlled and sv_audit_log both strictly NARROW. Two residuals, neither a finding against this change: the append-only lock is application-level because the schema still grants update on sv_audit_log to service_role (no delete grant anywhere on any sv_ table); and SV_RESOURCES is a plain object literal, so a prototype key such as constructor enters the gate block, gets NOT_SV rather than DENY, queries a table of that name, 404s and returns an empty provisioned answer -- harmless today, and worth noting only because SV_ROLE_MATRIX was given a null prototype for exactly this reason and SV_RESOURCES was not.

SURFACE 3, F4: THE GATE FIRES AND THE RECORD CARRIES NO CLAIM AT ALL. hank asks whether "reviewed by" is honest. The PRIOR question is whether there is a claim, and there is not. enforceAiApproval mutates payload; the rf_photos branch does not store payload -- it rebuilds the record from three named fields (photo_base64, a clamped ai_analysis, parsed_quantities) and persists that, and the redaction helper copies its input so it cannot reintroduce fields that were never there. grep -n "ai_source\|ai_approved" api/sd-data.js returns ONE line, a comment, and nothing else in the whole file. So ai_source, ai_approved_by and ai_approved_at NEVER REACH THE ROW. The consequence is the one the safeguard exists to prevent: aiFooter() short-circuits on a missing ai_source and returns the empty string, so the stored record renders NO FOOTER AT ALL -- not even the "AI-assisted, not reviewed" line that exists specifically so an absent footer and an unreviewed one cannot read the same. Nothing distinguishes an approved rf_photos row from a pre-change unflagged one. The ENFORCEMENT half works: no session still yields 403 AI_APPROVAL_REQUIRED. "The gate fired" and "the record says who approved it" have come apart, and only the first is true.

WHY NO ARM CAUGHT IT: two arms exist and neither can see it. One asserts the literal ai_source: appears in the client function's body -- a text test over the HTML. The other drives enforceAiApproval IN ISOLATION and asserts the LOCAL payload object was mutated. Neither routes rf_photos through api/sd-data.js. The end-to-end footer assertion does exist, on mech_quotes, whose branch stores the payload wholesale. The resource that was switched on is the one resource whose handler rebuilds the record, and the end-to-end arm was run on a different one.

ON THE HONESTY QUESTION hank ACTUALLY ASKED: the operator never sees the model prose. The raw reply is parked in a variable with four occurrences in the file -- declaration, reset, assignment, payload -- and is NEVER written to the DOM; the panel markup has no raw-text element and no AI label. What the operator confirms is the extracted numeric quantity form. hank's own disclosure is ACCURATE about the human act, and I accept it: the quantities are indeed what the estimate is built from. But the sentence's premise, that the footer will carry their name, is FALSE IN THIS BUILD -- there is no footer; and when there is one it interpolates the employee_id, not a name. ROUTED TO hank: carry the three provenance fields into the rebuilt record. ROUTED TO cody: an end-to-end arm that routes rf_photos through api/sd-data.js and asserts aiFooter() on the STORED record -- the arm that would have caught this. And one stale comment: api/sd-data.js still says no client stamps a high-risk resource today, which as of this change is false.

WHAT THIS DISCHARGE DOES NOT CLAIM. No suite was run. Surface 1's findings are read from source, not driven -- I did not POST alf_clients and then call family_mar, so F3 is a traced path and not an observed exploit. F4 is likewise traced, not observed: I did not write an rf_photos row and read it back. api/_resources/sairncare.js was examined only for which actions it registers, which is how the missing revoke was found, and not reviewed otherwise. The office_manager migration is disclosed in the schema as not run, and Michael has confirmed all six run-order blocks ran on Oct 14 19:38 ET, so that is recorded as CLOSED rather than raised. No api/, sql/, tools/ or tests/ file was touched and neither auditor clone was entered.

about. It is also the mirror of the harm F1 closed: F1 was sixty minutes unpaid
by omission; this is sixty minutes removed by commission, which is worse because
somebody chose it.
